messages.author: df2011c04ce6269d
messages.subject: multi_normal caused  segmentation fault
parts:
I'm using cmdstan. When I optimize the model. After showing configurations, it shows only one line error "Segmentation fault (core dumped)"
At the same time, sampling is accomplish without any problem.
My original model is complicated so I replace it with belows which shows actually the same error:

parameters{
  vector[2] a;
}

model{
  matrix[2,2] cov;
  vector[2] k;
  k[1] <- 0;
  k[2] <- 0;
  cov[1,1] <- 1;
  cov[1,2] <- 0.5;
  cov[2,1] <- 0.5;
  cov[2,2] <- 1;
  a ~ multi_normal(k, cov);
}

Any suggestion?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] multi_normal caused  segmentation fault
parts:
I think there's an issue somewhere in the optimization code
that we're trying to track down before the 2.6 release, which
should be soon.

An unrelated comment: If you have variables with fixed values,
as in cov and k here, it's better to define them in the transformed
data block for efficiency. Making them local variables in the model
turns them into parameter-like variables and derivatives of the log
prob with respect to them get calculated but are never needed.

- Bob

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] multi_normal caused segmentation fault
parts:
A chainable_alloc (LDLT_alloc in particular) is ending up on the var_alloc_stack twice for some reason, not at all sure why though.  The crash arises due to a double delete.  My current theory is that somewhere var_alloc_stack is not getting clear()d in the optimizers calling pattern, otherwise it should show up during sampling but I'm not sure where or how.

Cheers,
Marcus
